title: A method on one page
description: What in your session repeats and what rests only on you; the session in steps; testing the method on two people.

units.title: What repeats and what rests on you
The test: a method for two

objectives.text: Split your last three sessions into elements that repeat and elements that are personal
Describe a session in 4–7 steps, with the purpose and the time of each step
For each step, decide whether it holds two people at once and what to change in it

checks.question: Which of these is a repeatable part of the method?
options: The order of the session's steps
The intuition of which exercise to choose today
The history with a particular client
The tone of the leader's voice
checks.explain: The order of steps repeats in the same form even without you — an apprentice can repeat it. Intuition, history and tone are the personal part (u1, “Two parts of a session”).

checks.question: A leader described her session on three pages, with notes for each client. What is wrong?
options: Nothing: the more detail, the better
It is an instruction for one person; a method should fit on one page in 4–7 steps
A page about prices is missing
A method does not need to be described at all
checks.explain: Notes for each client are the personal part. A method is shorter than the practice: 4–7 steps on one page, each with an action, a purpose and minutes (u2, “One page is the limit”).

checks.question: Which session step most often does not hold two people without a change?
options: The question “what did you notice” at the end
Hands-on work fitted to one client's body
A short exercise to take home
checks.explain: Hands-on work needs all the attention on one body — it cannot be split between two. The breath, the shared question and the home exercise carry over (u3, worked example).
